description: InvokeHostFunction that deploys the Stellar Asset Contract for LWV2 through HOST_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_V2 (CAP-0058) with an asset preimage, the stellar_asset executable and no constructor arguments. Most tools deploy a SAC with CREATE_CONTRACT (v1); core and the host accept V2 as well. stellar-php-sdk 1.18.0 and stellar_flutter_sdk 3.12.0 re-encode the host function as CREATE_CONTRACT and so compute a wrong transaction hash (Soneso/stellar-php-sdk#252, Soneso/stellar_flutter_sdk#305).

core_version_and_commit.basis: the testnet network's core release as recorded for the other protocol-30 captures (RPC getVersionInfo); the data-lake emitter does not publish its core build, so this identifies the network's core release rather than the exact process that wrote the primary artifact

xdr_json.why: Horizon reports the function as HostFunctionTypeCreateContractV2
the SAC instance the deploy created

expected_state_changes_or_participants.indexer_must: read the host function type as decoded (CREATE_CONTRACT_V2) and never rebuild it from a model; hash the envelope bytes as they are
expected_state_changes_or_participants.note: the operation changes only the new contract instance and its TTL; the fee and sequence changes are transaction-level

validation_evidence.check: rs-stellar-xdr strict decode and byte-exact re-encode
ledger header hash recomputed from header bytes and matched to the recorded ledger hash
validation_evidence.method: ledgerwitness verify; ledger hash independently read from RPC getLedgers and from Horizon testnet /ledgers/5822970

validation_evidence.check: scp_value.tx_set_hash and tx_set_result_hash recomputed from the artifact
header signed by a pinned testnet validator
every envelope hashes under the declared passphrase to a processed result

validation_evidence.method: not applicable to network captures: core goldens are produced by core's own test suite under its test passphrase; see docs/spec/normalization.md

validation_evidence.check: same ledger fetched from RPC getLedgers is equal under stellar-core's --check-lcm normalization once the LCM extension is ignored
submitted envelope equals the envelope in the ledger
validation_evidence.method: byte comparison of the base64 envelope returned by the submitting script with focus-envelope.xdr

validation_evidence.check: transaction successful, source account and host function type as Horizon reports them; ledger transaction count
validation_evidence.method: GET horizon-testnet /transactions/{hash} (successful, source_account), /transactions/{hash}/operations (function HostFunctionTypeHostFunctionTypeCreateContractV2) and /ledgers/5822970 (4 successful plus 2 failed)

license_or_provenance_notes: Public testnet ledger data. Keys used to submit the focus transaction were generated per run, funded by friendbot and discarded; no secret material is stored.
